items.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015
items.q: I’ve had some wonderful opportunities to hang out with him and play music with him and talk with him on the phone and he was very supportive of me early on.

ctx.x: It’s still alive, which is great.

Yeah. And I’ve had some wonderful opportunities to hang out with him and play music with him and talk with him on the phone and he was very supportive of me early on. During my days with Woody Herman I know I still have a copy of it — there was an interview with him — Leonard Feather did an interview with him in the L.A. Times and when Leonard Feather asked him about new people coming up and he mentioned me and my writing and all that. And I was in New York and someone sent me the article and I saw it and I said…

just wrote him a letter, “thank you so much you’ve been a big influence over the years.” And he called me up. Out of the blue. Like shocking. I’d never met him before. So a really good guy and unbelievable technique. And when I was in high school was when his first big band records were coming out. And it was super-inspirational. Because kind of like Woody Herman with all the young guys, his group was kind of doing more like modern kind of Latin music and contemporary rock and things like that that were not…
